difficultyAxis: First CRUD tier: three entities in a two-level chain (Instructor <- Course <- Enrollment), nine scenarios, and one validation-heavy entity whose eight attributes mostly carry declarative rules. Update and delete appear here for the first time.
rationale: The visible step over tier 2 is the operation set: create, read, update and delete must all be emitted, and delete must distinguish an existing resource from a missing one. The chain Instructor <- Course <- Enrollment forces two foreign-key attributes to be carried through the model, repository and controller layers rather than one.

userStories.intent: register an instructor with a departmental contact address
userStories.benefit: courses can be assigned to a known teacher

scenarios.given: a non-empty instructor name and a well-formed email address
scenarios.then: the instructor is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.when: the registrar attempts to register the instructor
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: create a course for an existing instructor
userStories.benefit: the curriculum reflects who teaches what

scenarios.given: an existing instructor identifier and a credits value within the permitted range
scenarios.then: the course is persisted with its instructor reference intact

scenarios.given: a capacity below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the registrar attempts to create the course
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: enrol a student on an existing course
userStories.benefit: the student is registered for the term

scenarios.given: an existing course identifier and a well-formed student reference
scenarios.then: the enrolment is persisted with its course reference intact

scenarios.given: a course identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the administrator attempts to enrol the student
scenarios.then: the service reports the course as not found

userStories.intent: amend a course and remove an enrolment
userStories.benefit: the curriculum and the roll stay accurate

scenarios.given: an existing course and a new title
scenarios.then: the course is persisted with the new title and the previous values are replaced
the enrolment is removed and the read that follows reports it as not found

scenarios.given: an enrolment identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the administrator attempts to delete that enrolment
scenarios.then: the service reports the resource as not found
